title: The Petite Chaut and Mr. Lehmann
summary: The band took a regular but cheap job at the Petite Chaut under Mr. Lehmann while waiting six weeks for a Berlin contract.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: But he folded. And we were fortunate to find another job. This job was owned by -- it was called the Petite Chaut.
was a regular job. I mean, but he's taken advantage -- the proprietor was Mr. Raymond. He'd taken advantage of our situation to get us dirt cheap.

So, we didn't worry. We always had a certain sum of money in our pockets. We were not broke. But we figured there was no point in staying out of work until the Berlin contract comes up. We had about six weeks before.
So this was about Christmas, 1927, by this time?
Yes. Did we talk about Vienna at the
Weiburg Bar? With Dad Cook? Yes.
Well, we had two engagements, you see. We had a Berlin engagement for six months after.

Eight months after. Well, in any case from then on we accepted this contract with Mr. Lehmann which was a bona fide contract. It didn't pay much, but we were satisfied, and we went sightseeing and everything else.
